title: Patterns and edge-case reference for UI tokens, tables, charts, and migration checklist
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: Produce a focused reference doc for component authors and engineers that captures not only canonical usage for tokens, buttons, tables, and charts, but also non-obvious edge cases, accessibility callouts, visual regression guardrails, and a pragmatic migration checklist for the v2 token set and component APIs.

Scope:
- Usage patterns (recommended props/configs) for primary component families: Buttons, DataTable, PaginatedTable, Line/Bar charts.
- Do/don't guidance with screenshots/examples (where possible) and a short rationale.
- Edge-case catalog: truncated labels, dense rows, nested interactive controls, rtl and theming interactions.
- Token mapping table: legacy token -> v2 token equivalence + fallbacks for users who still use raw CSS variables.
- Migration checklist: codemod suggestions, quick-change rollout strategy, and monitoring signals to watch in Redwood Console (latency/cost not relevant here but visual regressions are).
- API doc highlights: props with backward-compat notes, known breaking changes, and helper utilities exposed in the library (e.g., useChartColorScale, resolveToken).

Why: Previous docs focused on component anatomy and broad patterns; they did not capture many small but high-impact edge cases we see in support tickets and regression PRs (e.g., charts that lose contrast in dark mode, tables with nested buttons that break keyboard focus order). This reference reduces repeated design reviews and prevents regressions during automated migrations.
acceptance_criteria: A single page in the docs site with sections for tokens, buttons, tables, and charts exists and is linkable from the Design System homepage
Each section includes at least two do/don't examples and one edge-case with explicit remediation steps
Token mapping table published as a downloadable CSV and included inline in the page
Migration checklist includes codemod command examples and a suggested canary rollout plan
PR template for visual regression contains pointers to the new examples and explicit accessibility checks
